c1-16-001.gate_key: adv_agree | C1 | gap | The number of applicants ___ fallen sharply this year. (have) |

item.q: The number of applicants ___ fallen sharply this year. (have)
item.why: *The number of* + plural noun takes a singular verb: the number is one thing. *The number of applicants has fallen.*
item.why_lv: *The number of* + daudzskaitlis prasa darbības vārdu vienskaitlī: skaitlis ir viena lieta. *The number of applicants has fallen.*

c1-16-002.gate_key: adv_agree | C1 | gap | A number of applicants ___ already withdrawn, so there are still places left. (have) |

item.q: A number of applicants ___ already withdrawn, so there are still places left. (have)
item.why: *A number of* = several, so the verb is plural: *A number of applicants have withdrawn.* Compare: *The number of applicants has fallen* (the number is one thing).
item.why_lv: *A number of* = vairāki, tāpēc darbības vārds ir daudzskaitlī (salīdzini: *The number of applicants has fallen*, skaitlis ir viena lieta): *A number of applicants have withdrawn.*

c1-16-003.gate_key: adv_agree | C1 | gap | Politics ___ never interested me much, but this election is different. (have) |

item.q: Politics ___ never interested me much, but this election is different. (have)
item.why: *politics* ends in *-s* but takes a singular verb: *Politics has never interested me.*
item.why_lv: *politics* beidzas ar *-s*, bet darbības vārds ir vienskaitlī: *Politics has never interested me.*

c1-16-004.gate_key: adv_agree | C1 | gap | The criteria for the award ___ changed this year, so please read them again. (have) |

item.q: The criteria for the award ___ changed this year, so please read them again. (have)
item.why: *criteria* is the plural of *criterion*: *The criteria have changed.*

c1-16-005.gate_key: adv_agree | C1 | gap | Write one word in the gap: We need two more chairs, because the manager and two of her assistants ___ coming to the meeting tomorrow. |

item.q: Write one word in the gap: We need two more chairs, because the manager and two of her assistants ___ coming to the meeting tomorrow.
item.why: With *and*, the subject is plural: *The manager and two of her assistants are coming.* With *together with*, it stays singular: *The manager, together with two of her assistants, is coming.*
item.why_lv: Ar *and* teikuma priekšmets ir daudzskaitlī: *The manager and two of her assistants are coming.* Ar *together with* tas paliek vienskaitlī: *The manager, together with two of her assistants, is coming.*

c1-16-006.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Despite the traffic, we could catch the last bus.

key.correct: Despite the traffic, we could catch the last bus.
wrong: I could hear the neighbours arguing all night.
We couldn't find a parking space anywhere.
After three tries, she managed to open the jar.

item.why: For one achievement on one occasion, use *were able to* or *managed to*, not *could*: *Despite the traffic, we were able to catch the last bus.* *could* is fine for a general ability, with verbs like *hear*, and in the negative (*couldn't find*).
item.why_lv: Vienam *paveikumam* vienā reizē lieto *were able to* vai *managed to*, nevis *could*: *Despite the traffic, we were able to catch the last bus.* *could* der vispārējai spējai, ar tādiem darbības vārdiem kā *hear* un noliegumā (*couldn't find*).
item.correct: Despite the traffic, we could catch the last bus.
wrong: I could hear the neighbours arguing all night.
We couldn't find a parking space anywhere.
After three tries, she managed to open the jar.

c1-16-007.gate_key: adv_part | C1 | gap | ___ with the other candidates, she was clearly the strongest. (compare) |

item.q: ___ with the other candidates, she was clearly the strongest. (compare)
item.why: The candidate is the one being compared, so the participle is passive: *Compared with the other candidates, she was…* Compare *Judging by the queue*: there the speaker judges.
item.why_lv: Kandidāte *tiek* salīdzināta ar *citiem*, tāpēc 3. forma ir ciešamajā kārtā: *Compared with the other candidates, she was*… Salīdzini ar *Judging by the queue*: tur spriež runātājs.

c1-16-008.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | Show that the shouting went on for a long time: His voice was hoarse because he ___ all afternoon at the match. (shout) |

item.q: Show that the shouting went on for a long time: His voice was hoarse because he ___ all afternoon at the match. (shout)
item.why: The shouting was over and explains how his voice was later: past perfect continuous, *had been shouting* (*shouted* and *had shouted* are possible too, but they do not show how long it went on).
item.why_lv: Kliegšana jau bija beigusies un izskaidro, kāda vēlāk bija viņa balss: Past Perfect Continuous, *had been shouting* (iespējami arī *shouted* un *had shouted*, bet *tie* neparāda, cik ilgi tas turpinājās).

c1-16-009.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | text | Report what she said with *deny* and *having*. Her words: 'I didn't read the letter.' |

accepted: She denied having read the letter.

item.q: Report what she said with *deny* and *having*. Her words: 'I didn't read the letter.'
item.why: *deny* + *having* + 3rd form for something earlier than the denying: *She denied having read the letter.* (*She denied reading the letter* is natural too, but this task asks for *having*.)
item.why_lv: *deny + having* + 3. forma tam, kas notika pirms noliegšanas: *She denied having read the letter.* (*Dabiski* ir arī *She denied reading the letter*, bet šis *uzdevums* prasa *having*.)
answers: She denied having read the letter.

c1-16-010.gate_key: adv_prep | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: She took a bookkeeping course ___ her own business. | with a view to starting

wrong: with a view to start
with a view of starting
in view to starting

item.q: Choose the correct option: She took a bookkeeping course ___ her own business.
item.why: The fixed phrase is *with a view to* + *-ing* (*to* here is a preposition): *with a view to starting her own business*.
item.why_lv: Nemainīgais izteiciens ir *with a view to + -ing* (*to* te ir prievārds): *with a view to starting her own business*.
wrong: with a view to start
with a view of starting
in view to starting

c1-16-011.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | mcq | In this story, which verb gives the background, not an event that moves the story on? So I'm sitting on the train, this man opens a bag of crisps, and the whole carriage turns round. | 'm sitting

wrong: opens
turns round
all three

item.q: In this story, which verb gives the background, not an event that moves the story on? So I'm sitting on the train, this man opens a bag of crisps, and the whole carriage turns round.
item.why: In a story told in the present, the background is usually in the present continuous (*I'm sitting on the train*) and the events that move the story on are in the present simple (*opens, turns round*).
item.why_lv: Stāstā tagadnē fons parasti ir Present Continuous (*I'm sitting on the train*), bet notikumi, kas *virza* stāstu, ir Present Simple (*opens, turns round*).
wrong: opens
turns round
all three

answer_notes: The lawyer demanded that her client should be told the whole truth.

c1-16-013.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Years ago, the factory would be where the car park is now.

key.correct: Years ago, the factory would be where the car park is now.
wrong: Whenever we visited my uncle, we would play in his garden.
Didn't you use to have red hair?
We visited Switzerland four times in the nineties.

item.why: For a past state that has changed, use *used to*, not *would*: *Years ago, the factory used to be where the car park is now.*
item.why_lv: Pagātnes stāvoklim, kas mainījies, lieto *used to*, nevis *would*: *Years ago, the factory used to be where the car park is now.*
